Successful-schedule-then-crash window before the `scheduled: true` update can re-send SMS and retrigger retry machinery (pre-existing issue interacting with new retry logic)

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteMany OR-branch loses method and scheduledDate scoping, allowing deletion of live future reminders of any method with retryCount > 1, causing unrecoverable data loss
Retry cap implemented by silently hard-deleting the reminder row instead of marking it failed, so failures are swallowed with no persisted record

adjudication.rationale: The diff implements a retry cap by deleting records via `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`, which hard-deletes reminders once `retryCount > 1` rather than persisting a failed/terminal state. This does indeed remove any record of repeated failures (and the delete condition isn’t tied to SMS or scheduledDate), but whether that is a correctness bug vs an intentional cleanup/observability tradeoff isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retryCount is incremented on all failures including non-retryable ones and the 'no SMS record' branch, with no distinction between retryable and terminal errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `retryCount` is incremented unconditionally both when `scheduledSMS` is falsy (the new `else` branch) and for any thrown error (the `catch`), with no branching on error type or terminal conditions. However, the diff alone does not establish which failures are non-retryable vs retryable, so this is a valid, diff-grounded concern about missing distinction rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retryCount update inside the catch block can itself throw, aborting the whole loop and skipping remaining reminders (per-reminder failure becomes batch-wide abort)

adjudication.rationale: In the per-reminder loop, the `catch (error)` block now does `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` to increment `retryCount`. That update is not wrapped in its own try/catch, so if it throws (e.g., DB error, record missing), the exception will escape the catch block and abort the handler, preventing remaining reminders from being processed. This creates batch-wide failure from a single reminder error, introduced by the new catch-block update logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount (computed as retryCount + 1 from stale fetched value instead of increment: { retryCount: 1 }), risking lost increments under concurrent cron runs and SMS over-sending
matched_golden_ids: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same concurrency bug: retryCount is updated via non-atomic read-modify-write (retryCount + 1) using a potentially stale value, which can lose increments under concurrent runs, and suggests using Prisma's atomic increment instead. This matches the golden comment (including the broader concurrency concern).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one boundary on retry cap: retryCount: { gt: 1 } allows 3 total attempts before deletion instead of the intended 2

adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes reminders with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` (i.e., retryCount >= 2) at the start of the handler. Since `retryCount` starts at 0 and is incremented by 1 on each failed scheduling attempt, a reminder is attempted at retryCount 0 (1st attempt) and retryCount 1 (2nd attempt); after the second failure it becomes 2 and will be deleted on the next run before any 3rd attempt. So `gt: 1` enforces 2 total attempts, not 3.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unscoped deleteMany OR clause on retryCount is not constrained by method: SMS, deleting non-SMS reminders and causing data loss
matched_golden_ids: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that a deleteMany OR clause using retryCount is not scoped to method: SMS, which can delete non-SMS reminders (data loss). This is the same underlying bug described in the golden comment: missing WorkflowMethods.SMS filter within the retryCount deletion condition causing unintended deletion of Email/WhatsApp reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retried reminders exceeding retryCount 1 are hard-deleted instead of being marked failed/cancelled, silently dropping reminders after failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the cleanup `deleteMany` to hard-delete any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` via an `OR` clause, regardless of method/status/date. Since retryCount is incremented on failures (both in the `else` branch and `catch`), reminders that fail twice will be deleted on the next run without being marked failed/cancelled, effectively dropping them silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-reminder update calls in the loop create N+1 writes with no batching, multiplying DB load during outages

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-reminder `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls inside the loop: once in the new `else` branch when scheduling doesn’t produce a `scheduledSMS.sid`, and again in the `catch` block (both increment `retryCount`). This creates one DB write per reminder processed, which can amplify DB load when many reminders fail (e.g., during an SMS provider outage). It’s a performance/operational concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteMany filter on retryCount has no index, degrading to a broader scan on every job run

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `retryCount` column (default 0) and changes `deleteMany` to include an `OR` branch filtering `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`. In `schema.prisma`, `WorkflowReminder` only shows indexes on `bookingUid` and `workflowStepId`, with no index on `retryCount`, so this new deletion path may require scanning more rows and could degrade performance on each job run. This is a performance/ops concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New OR branch in deleteMany drops the method filter and date constraint, deleting successfully-scheduled SMS reminders (silent data loss) without cancelling the Twilio message

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteMany` condition adds an `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without any `method`/`scheduledDate`/“unscheduled” constraints, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`. In the scheduling loop, on success the update sets `referenceId` etc. but does not reset `retryCount` to 0, so a reminder that previously failed twice and later succeeds can still have `retryCount > 1` and be deleted on the next run. There is also no Twilio cancellation logic shown, so this can lead to silent DB data loss while an SMS remains scheduled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The OR'd retryCount > 1 condition isn't scoped to SMS method, so non-SMS reminders could be swept if retryCount is set elsewhere

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteMany`, the `OR` includes `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without also scoping `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. That means *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` (including non-SMS methods) would be deleted by this handler, which is broader than the prior SMS-only deletion and could cause unintended data loss for other reminder types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Successful retries never reset retryCount to 0, leaving stale retryCount on a scheduled reminder that can later trigger deletion

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a scenario where a successfully scheduled reminder’s non-zero retryCount would later cause deletion. retryCount is only incremented on failure, and deleteMany only deletes records with retryCount > 1. With this handler’s flow, once a reminder reaches retryCount=2 it will be deleted at the start of the next run before it can ever succeed, so no scheduled reminder can end up with retryCount>1. A scheduled reminder might retain retryCount=1 after a prior failure, but that does not meet the deletion condition shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Failed reminders are hard-deleted after retries instead of marked failed, leaving no notification to booking owner and no audit trail

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces hard deletion of reminders based on retryCount: deleteMany now includes an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` (not even scoped to SMS), so once failures increment `retryCount` (new updates in both the `else` after scheduling and the `catch`), the record will be physically removed on the next run rather than being retained/marked failed. This removes any audit trail of failed reminders, consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteMany OR clause deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduled date, destroying future pending reminders

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the initial `deleteMany` was meant to remove past-due SMS reminders (`scheduledDate.lte(now)` with `method: SMS`). The diff changes the `where` to an `OR` that includes `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `scheduledDate` constraint. That will delete *any* reminder with `retryCount > 1`, including those scheduled in the future, which can destroy pending reminders and contradicts the comment/intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteMany retryCount > 1 filter is not scoped to method SMS, so other reminder types with retry tracking would be silently deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The `retryCount > 1` branch is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this handler will delete any `WorkflowReminder` rows of other methods once their `retryCount` exceeds 1, causing unintended data loss beyond SMS reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminders are deleted rather than marked failed when retries exceed limit, with no audit trail or rollback mechanism

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly deletes reminders when `retryCount` exceeds a threshold: `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. At the same time, failures increment `retryCount` via `update({ data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }})`. This means reminders that have failed multiple times will be removed from the database on the next run, rather than being retained/marked as failed. Whether this is a defect depends on product requirements, but the concern about losing an audit trail is grounded in the new deletion condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retryCount increment uses read-then-write (retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of atomic { increment: 1 }, causing races under concurrent cron runs

adjudication.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` via a read-then-write (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in two `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls. Since `reminder.retryCount` comes from a prior query, concurrent executions updating the same row can lose increments (last writer wins). Using Prisma’s atomic update (`{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`) would avoid this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent handlers can double-increment or skip retryCount values, leading to premature deletion or extra retries

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates `retryCount` using a read-modify-write pattern (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in two places (the `else` branch and `catch`). Since `unscheduledReminders` are read without any lock/transaction and the increment is not atomic (no Prisma `increment` operator), concurrent handler executions processing the same reminder can race and write an incorrect `retryCount` (e.g., both read 0 and both write 1, losing an increment). Because `retryCount` is then used for deletion (`deleteMany` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`), an incorrect count can change retry/deletion behavior (extra retries or, depending on interleavings, premature deletion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Catch block increments retryCount without idempotency guard while reminder remains scheduled, so persistently failing reminders are re-fetched and incremented every run

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, failures (either `else` when no `sid`, or the `catch`) update the reminder with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` but do not change any other field that would exclude the record from the next run’s fetch (the query still selects reminders by `scheduledDate` window). This means a reminder that keeps failing will be re-processed on each handler run and `retryCount` will keep increasing until the top-of-handler `deleteMany` removes it via `retryCount > 1`. That behavior is visible in the diff; whether it is incorrect depends on intended retry/idempotency semantics (not provable from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No terminal failure state (e.g., isFailed flag) exists; give-up mechanism is silent deletion and failures are only logged via console.log, invisible to operators

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a retryCount and a give-up mechanism that deletes records when retryCount > 1 via deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } }). There is no terminal failure marker (no isFailed/status field) added, and failures are only surfaced via console.log in the catch; after exceeding retries the reminder can be silently deleted with no persisted failure state for operators to query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PartialWorkflowReminder type cast means retryCount may be undefined for other consumers, risking NaN

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the query explicitly selects `retryCount: true` and the result is cast to `(PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[]`, so within this code path `reminder.retryCount` is expected to be present. Additionally, the migration adds `retryCount` as `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so existing rows should have a concrete numeric value, avoiding `undefined`/`NaN` in `reminder.retryCount + 1`. The finding’s claim about `PartialWorkflowReminder` causing `retryCount` to be undefined for other consumers is not evidenced by the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing max-retry constant; retry ceiling is implicit and undocumented

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the retry ceiling in query logic (`deleteMany` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) and increments `retryCount` on failures (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`). This effectively encodes a max-retry policy (delete after >1) without a named constant or in-code documentation, making the limit implicit and harder to maintain/change, but not a clear functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retryCount > 1 deletion branch in deleteMany has no `method` filter, so it hard-deletes non-SMS (e.g., email) reminders and also lacks cancelled/bookingUid guards

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteMany`, the new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not constrained by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or any other scoping), so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1`, including non-SMS reminders, which is an unintended broad hard-delete risk. The diff clearly shows this widened predicate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When retry budget is exhausted, reminders are hard-deleted with no log, status flag, or audit record, causing silent data loss; should mark failed/cancelled instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and then hard-deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1` via `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })` with no accompanying status flag/audit trail in the shown code. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about observability/data retention, but it’s not provably a functional defect (it may be intended cleanup behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retry counter increment is non-atomic (uses value read at query time instead of `{ increment: 1 }`), losing updates under concurrent cron runs and risking duplicate SMS sends

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and increments it via `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in two places (the `else` branch after scheduling attempt and in `catch`). Since `reminder.retryCount` was read earlier in the `findMany` result, this is a read-modify-write update that is non-atomic. If the handler can run concurrently (e.g., overlapping cron runs) or multiple workers process the same reminder, increments can be lost because two updates may both write the same computed value instead of using an atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Catch block treats all exceptions as retryable, including permanent failures like Twilio auth errors, which can cascade into mass deletion of all pending reminders on the next run

adjudication.rationale: The new logic increments `retryCount` for any non-success response and for *all* exceptions in the `catch` block (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`), with no distinction between transient and permanent failures. On subsequent runs, the startup `deleteMany` now deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` (second OR branch), which will purge reminders that repeatedly fail due to a persistent/permanent error. This creates a clear path to data loss (reminders dropped after repeated failures).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Successful-schedule-then-crash window before the `scheduled: true` update can re-send SMS and retrigger retry machinery (pre-existing issue interacting with new retry logic)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an external side-effect (scheduling SMS) followed by a separate Prisma update marking the reminder scheduled (and setting referenceId). If the process crashes after the SMS is successfully scheduled but before `prisma.workflowReminder.update({... scheduled: true ...})`, the reminder remains "unscheduled" in DB and will be picked up again in a later run, potentially sending a duplicate SMS. With the new `retryCount` logic (increment on failure/else; deletion when `retryCount > 1` via the new `deleteMany` OR clause), subsequent runs can also start incrementing/deleting the reminder even though an SMS may already have been scheduled, compounding the inconsistency. This race window/idempotency gap is visible from the non-atomic external call + DB update pattern in the diff.
